heading: EXT. MONASTERY ORCHARD - TRENCH LINE - EVENING

units.text: EXT. MONASTERY ORCHARD - TRENCH LINE - EVENING
A line of earth cut through rows of apple trees, their blossoms falling like a slow snow into the mud.
Beyond the wall, the white stones of a ruined abbey.
The sky is the colour of old pewter.
Everything is hushed, as though the war has paused to breathe.
LT. HENRI DUBOIS, 30s, sits on an upturned crate at the lip of the trench, a bandage around his left hand, scribbling in a notebook.
Thin as a rake, with a poet's brow and a smoker's cough.
SGT. ALBERT QUIGLEY, 50s, a barrel-chested veteran with a drooping moustache, squats beside a battered kettle over a spirit stove.
He fusses with the tea, humming under his breath.
PVT.
SANTIAGO MORALES, 20, round-faced, sits on the firing step with a harmonica he does not play.
He turns it over and over in his hands.
CPL.
JOSEPH WHITEFEATHER, 30s, tall, quiet, leans against the trench wall cleaning a rifle with a rag, eyes half-closed, a long braid down his back.
Tea's nearly ready.
units.name: QUIGLEY

units.text: Lovely.
units.name: DUBOIS

units.text: It's terrible tea.
units.name: QUIGLEY

units.text: Then it's British.
units.name: DUBOIS

units.text: I'm from Leeds, sir. It's worse than British.
units.name: QUIGLEY

units.text: Morales lifts the harmonica to his lips, hesitates, lowers it.
Whitefeather glances over without comment, then returns to the rifle.
A petal drifts into the kettle.
Quigley fishes it out with a finger.
Sergeant, is it true what they say about the orchard?
units.name: MORALES

units.text: What do they say?
units.name: QUIGLEY

units.text: That the monks planted these trees four hundred years ago.
units.name: MORALES

units.text: Five hundred.
units.name: QUIGLEY

units.text: Closer to six, I believe. The brothers kept records.
units.name: DUBOIS

units.text: Records of what?
units.name: MORALES

units.text: Of every harvest. Every frost. Every war that passed through.
units.name: DUBOIS

units.text: Did they write about us?
units.name: WHITEFEATHER

units.text: Not yet.
units.name: DUBOIS

units.text: A rumble far off, then silence again.
The four men listen.

A single blackbird begins to sing from the abbey wall, and Morales finally plays three soft notes on the harmonica before dropping his hand, embarrassed, while Quigley pours the tea into dented tin mugs, hands one to Dubois, one to Whitefeather, one to Morales, and settles back on his heels with the last mug warming his palms, all of them listening to the bird as the light goes slowly copper over the blossoming wall.
Funny thing.
units.name: QUIGLEY

units.text: Mm?
units.name: DUBOIS

units.text: I've never heard a bird sing in a war before.
units.name: QUIGLEY

units.text: They only sing when it's over.
units.name: WHITEFEATHER

units.text: It's not over.
units.name: QUIGLEY

units.text: No.
units.name: WHITEFEATHER

units.text: The blackbird sings on.
Dubois closes his notebook and lifts his mug in a small salute to the trees.
